newsitem.title: UK: JERSEY BANK DEPOSITS FALL 1.9 PCT IN 2Q.
newsitem.headline: JERSEY BANK DEPOSITS FALL 1.9 PCT IN 2Q.

text.p: Bank deposits on the island of Jersey fell 1.9 percent to 89.2 billion stg in the second quarter, the States of Jersey financial services department said on Tuesday.
It said the fall was largely caused by a drop in the value of foreign currency accounts, which dropped 1.85 billion stg to 59.97 billion.

"Despite the drop in the sterling value of deposits, over half the banks in the island increased their deposit base during the second quarter," said Roger Bignell, Jersey's deputy director of banking.
Two new banking licences were approved during the quarter. These were to Australia New Zealand Banking Group and Alpha Credit Bank.
